Skills catalog

Three public orchestrators open the doors. Private primitives do the steps underneath.
Full reference on GitHub.

Public orchestrators

Architect, Builder, Craftsman — three entrypoints. Pick the outcome you need.
SkillWhat it does
/architect-system-foundationPropose a new system and scaffold it after you approve — or document what already exists. Rerun to keep docs in sync.
/build-requested-specTurn a natural-language request into one spec that owns its requirements, then implement, prove, and ship.
/craft-lasting-qualityReview quality, record technical debt, and repair one coherent slice through the same delivery flow.

The private primitives

The steps those three commands use. Run one when you want a single step.
SkillWhat it does
/outline-systemMap the system from the code: architecture, model, and the records a delivery needs.
/rule-projectExtract each project's rules and the commands it actually runs.
/define-specWrite one spec that owns its requirements, then pause for your approval.
/implement-projectWrite the code and tests for one project, and check this spec's acceptance along the way.
/verify-behaviorThe acceptance evidence. Green ships; red goes back for repair.
/review-implementationAn expert look at what linters miss. Findings become debt and do not block the release.
/scan-qualityA system-wide quality pass that refreshes the debt list.
/ship-specVersion the product, update the changelog, and merge.

Human checkpoints

You review at key moments. Everything else runs without asking — or skip stops with YOLO.|
TriggerYou check
During /architect-system-foundationThe proposed system, when the repo has no application source yet
During /build-requested-specThe spec and its requirements — unless you include YOLO
During /craft-lasting-qualityWhich coherent group of debt becomes the next repair, if any
flowchart LR
  A[architect-system-foundation] --> B[build-requested-spec]
  Q[craft-lasting-quality] --> B
  B -->|you ✔️ spec| S[implement → verify → review → ship]
